rv.q: Mirza’s new work can best be categorized as a dramedy, though the comedic elements come off more successfully than the domestic drama at its core.
“Neighborhood Watch” is a faithful and hilarious portrayal of the modern U.S. socio-political landscape.
In “Neighborhood Watch,” Mirza scores light-hearted laughs at the expense of white liberal culture and the racism of a different sort that can thrive among.
Mirza's script is a concise examination of consciousness in a time when we can become easily complacent in our day-to-day lives.
All in all, this play has a very good future.
What it lacks is nuance, subtlety and any semblance of believability.

cn.t: This sitcom-styled dramedy about liberal paranoia and prejudice in post-2024 suburbia earns mostly positive reviews for its timely premise and performances, though critics split on whether it successfully balances comedy with drama.
